correctness.rationale: On c₀, AP_m has finite rank, and for compact K the norm ||K Q_m|| tends to zero because K* has compact image of the ℓ₁ unit ball and ℓ₁ tails tend uniformly to zero on compact sets. This proves the input-tail formula by comparison to arbitrary K. Iteration of |[S+z(T−S)]x|≤T|x| for |z|<1, applied to Q_m x, then bounds the Calkin norms of all powers by the corresponding powers of T. Gelfand gives the claimed spectral disks without assuming the interpolated operator is positive. For r>0 the spectral mapping of (1+conj(λ/r)G(z))/2 and Vesentini give equality of its radius with one throughout the disk, forcing persistence of λ/r by equality in the triangle inequality. Invertibility is open at z=1. At r=0, nonempty spectra of the unital Calkin algebra lie in {0}, so the result is automatic. The Fredholm interpretation follows from Atkinson. No computation is required.

evidence: Dobrick Corollary 2.5 gives equal-radius peripheral inclusion for positive ordered operators on an arbitrary complex Banach lattice. Theorem 2.3 even gives boundary constancy along the open unit disk interpolation.

Räbiger–Wolff Corollary 1.5 assumes (G)-solvability when working with ordinary spectra, and their Theorem 3.1 uses a Riesz-point hypothesis for an essential-radius conclusion. The Martínez title identifies essential-radius domination, but no full result from that paper was obtained.

evidence: For A on c₀, A** induces Â on the complex Banach lattice ℓ∞/c₀. Let a_i∈ℓ₁ be the rows of A; their fixed columns tend to zero. The output-tail formula gives ||A||_e=limsup_i||a_i||₁ since P_m A is finite-rank and Q_m K→0 in norm for every compact K.

The induced norm is exactly this limsup. It is at most the essential norm (compact maps act trivially in the quotient). For the converse, choose rows tending to the limsup and successive disjoint finite column blocks: pick each later row with arbitrarily small mass on the old finite prefix, and extend the block until its remaining row tail is small. A single bounded input, with conjugate phases of each chosen row on its block, then attains the limsup asymptotically on those rows, up to errors tending to zero.

It preserves the peripheral spectrum because exterior resolvents belong to the Calkin image; if an outer-circle point is invertible in the ambient algebra, approach it radially from outside and use continuity of the inverse and closedness of the image. The converse follows from the unital homomorphism. Both positivity and the order of S,T are preserved under the action on the quotient lattice.

originality.rationale: The result is a direct c₀ corollary of Dobrick's general theorem for positive operators on complex Banach lattices via the canonical action on ℓ∞/c₀. It is also obtained by applying Dobrick's precise Banach-algebra boundary persistence proposition to the Calkin interpolation after the elementary tail bound. The ordinary-spectrum versus essential-spectrum terminology does not prevent implication; the quotient preserves the relevant spectra. This is a finding of prior mathematical coverage, not of incorrectness or an inference from an inaccessible source.
